# Intake Brief: Configured test gate excludes the herdr package suite (no herdr test type/group) (WL-0MVGJ4WSS005BMSI)

## Headline

Add a sanctioned `herdr` test type (`run_tests.py --type herdr`) and a `herdr` named group (`--group herdr`) mapped to `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src`, so the herdr package suite (107 files / ~3,500 tests) runs through the test skill's runner and cache instead of ad-hoc vitest invocations — while **keeping herdr out of the canonical full gate**, honouring the prior producer decision on WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8.

## Problem statement

`.pi/test-config.json` declares the full suite as `npm --silent test -- tests/cli` + `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`. The `packages/herdr/src/*.test.ts` suite is therefore never run by any gate, and `run_tests.py --type herdr` fails with an unknown-type error because no local type/group defines it. Child sessions work around this with ad-hoc `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src` runs, which bypass the test skill's sanctioned runner and cache — so the audit cannot see the evidence and a red herdr tree can be pushed to `dev` undetected (WL-0MVFRALLB0065UIW was caught only by a direct vitest run).

## Users

- **Herdr work-item developers** (e.g. WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS AC6/AC8) — need a sanctioned, cache-recording way to run the herdr suite.
  - *User story:* As a herdr work-item developer, when I need to verify herdr changes, I want `run_tests.py --type herdr` to run the package suite and record a cache entry, so the audit can see my evidence without me invoking vitest ad hoc.
- **Producer / reviewer** — wants gate behaviour documented and evidence visible.
  - *User story:* As a producer, I want the documentation to state which suites the dev-push gate runs and how to run the herdr suite, so gate expectations are no longer ambiguous.
- **Implement skill** — wants changed-scope selection to pick the herdr suite for herdr-touching items.
  - *User story:* As the implement skill, when changed files are under `packages/herdr/`, I want the changed-scope gate to map to the `herdr` group, so finish-time validation targets exactly the affected suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `python3 run_tests.py --type herdr --json` (default scope `full`) resolves to `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src`, executes it, and records a cache entry under the `herdr` type key — a repeat invocation within the 2h TTL is served from cache (`cached: true`) and never satisfies the audit's full-suite query (only `--type full` scope `full` entries do).
- AC2: `python3 run_tests.py --group herdr --json` also works via a `groups.herdr` entry in `.pi/test-config.json`, and the group's `paths: ["packages/herdr/**"]` makes implement.py's changed-scope gate auto-select the herdr group when a change touches `packages/herdr/` (SA-0MUJKF2HP001BR51). Both type and group land in this item per D2.
- AC3: The canonical full suite is **unchanged** — `run_tests.py --type full` still runs exactly `tests/cli` + `tests/unit`; herdr is **not** added to `suiteCommands` (producer decision WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 preserved and documented).
- AC4: Extension contract held: `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` defines `types.herdr`; minimum types it omits (`unit`/`smoke`) fail with the runner's loud diagnostic (never a silent full-suite substitution), and `--type full` still works via the suiteCommands fallback.
- AC5 (validation): A verification step proves AC1–AC4: run `--type herdr` twice (first cold, second cached), `--group herdr`, `--type full` unchanged, and `--type unit`/`--type smoke` produce the expected loud diagnostics.
- AC6 (docs): The dev-gate documentation (`docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`, new **Test gates** section, cross-linked from `packages/herdr/README.md` "Run tests") states which suites the dev-push gate runs and how to run the herdr suite (`--type herdr` / `--group herdr`), and records the producer decision that herdr stays out of the full gate.
- AC7 (docs): All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes — code comments, `.pi/test-config.json`/extension file comments, README and any relevant wiki/docs entries. (CHANGELOG.md excluded.)
- AC8 (full suite): The full project test suite passes with the new changes (canonical gate green and untouched).

## Constraints

- **Producer decision (hard constraint):** herdr tests must **not** join the canonical full suite — WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 closed Won't fix: "the herdr tests will not be run as part of the canonical full suite". Cost of adding ~12–19 min per gate (item estimate) and observed flaky/order-dependent failures in 2026-10-20 runs justify a separate, opt-in gate.
- **Extension contract:** a local extension with a `types` map that omits a minimum type (`unit`/`smoke`) makes that type fail loudly (never silent full-suite substitution, AC4). Today `--type unit` already fails via convention (no pytest/`.mjs` in `tests/unit`), so the extension introduces no functional regression — the diagnostic text changes, which must be verified.
- **Suite command:** `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src` (vitest path filter) — the command verified in WL-0MVFE1IRB0004X1U.
- **Audit evidence scope:** `herdr`-type and `group:herdr` cache entries are **not** audit-accepted full-suite evidence (SA-0MT6BYQHB008DOGC). Audits of herdr-only items still require operator attestation (`--green-run HEAD`) or extended audit support (out of scope here — follow-up opportunity).
- **Runtime estimate discrepancy:** the work item says ~12–19 min; WL-0MVFE1IRB0004X1U measured ~130 s standalone (107 files / 3,510 tests, idle host). Re-measure at implementation start and record the figure in the doc update.

## Existing state

- `.pi/test-config.json`: `suiteCommands` = `tests/cli` + `tests/unit`; no `groups` key.
- No `.pi/skills_extensions/test/` directory; `run_tests.py --type herdr` → "Unknown test type 'herdr'" error.
- Repo `.githooks/pre-push` runs branch policy + context budget + `wl sync` only — it does **not** run the test suite (the framework's test-gated pre-push is not installed here); the test gate runs via `implement.py finish` changed-scope and the `ship` release gate, both reading `full_suite_commands`.

## Desired change

1. Create `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` with `{"types": {"herdr": ["npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src"]}}`.
2. Add `"groups": {"herdr": {"commands": ["npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src"], "paths": ["packages/herdr/**"]}}` to `.pi/test-config.json` (keeps `suiteCommands` untouched).
3. Document the gates and the herdr invocation in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (new **Test gates** section) and cross-link from `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` — NEW: `types.herdr` type map (`npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src`).
- `.pi/test-config.json` — ADD `groups.herdr` (commands + `paths: ["packages/herdr/**"]`); leave `suiteCommands` unchanged.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — ADD "Test gates" section: suites the dev-push gate runs, how to run herdr, producer decision on the full gate.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — ADD "Run the suite via the sanctioned runner" note (`run_tests.py --type herdr` / `--group herdr`).
- Tests: no new source tests required for JSON config; verification is command-level (AC5). If the repo's test conventions require unit tests for config, add minimal ones under `tests/`.

## Related work

- WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 (completed, Won't fix) — same underlying problem (herdr excluded from canonical suite); producer decided herdr does **not** join the full gate. This item fills the remaining gap: sanctioned type/group + docs, without overturning that decision.
- WL-0MVFE1IRB0004X1U (completed) — full herdr suite verification (107 files / 3,510 tests, ~130 s standalone); confirms the exact suite command.
- WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS (open, plan_complete) — herdr audit-dispatch feature whose AC6/AC8 require the herdr suite; immediate beneficiary.
- WL-0MVFRALLB0065UIW (completed test-failure) — herdr regression found only via ad-hoc vitest; evidence of the gap.
- WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR (open, intake_complete) — sibling item: *Canonical test suite excludes 76 root-level `tests/*.test.ts` files*; same gap family, different excluded set (`tests/*` root files vs `packages/herdr/src`). Complementary, not overlapping; both may touch the same doc target below.
- Framework test-skill docs (`skill/test/docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`, `skill-extensions.md` in the framework repo) — type-map and groups contract; SA-0MUJKF2HP001BR51, SA-0MTJQB2MA008HMO6.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Decision (documented, not blocking):** herdr stays a **separate gate** (type/group), not part of the full `suiteCommands` — honours the explicit producer decision on WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8. Producer may override; recorded in the Appendix.
- **Changed-scope interaction:** adding `groups.herdr` changes implement.py finish behaviour for herdr-touching items — finish runs only the herdr group, not the canonical changed-scope subset (which is deferred to the dev-push gate). This is the intended "gate invoked by items that touch it"; the canonical suite is still enforced by the dev-push/ship gates for repos with the framework pre-push installed. Mitigation: AC6 documents this and the repo's pre-push currently does **not** run the suite at all — a pre-existing gap worth a follow-up item (scope-creep guard: do not fix it here).
- **Current tree state:** an environment run at 2026-10-20 18:10 observed 3 failures + 2 unhandled errors in `worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts` and `worklist-blocked-by-cache.test.ts` (timing/order-sensitive, Green-circle and Blocked By rendering) — treat the herdr suite as potentially red at this moment; re-verify before relying on `--type herdr` evidence during implementation.
- **Runtime discrepancy (~130 s vs 12–19 min):** re-measure; record ground truth in the docs.
- **Audit evidence gap:** herdr-type entries aren't full-suite evidence; follow-up: teach the audit/`query_cached` to consult the `herdr` group entry for herdr-touching items (record as `discovered-from:WL-0MVGJ4WSS005BMSI`, do NOT do it in this item).
- **Scope creep guard:** `tests/herdr/` (20 files), `tests/bench`, `tests/integration`, etc. remain outside this item — only `packages/herdr/src` per the seed intent; further suite-extensions become follow-up items.
- **Shared doc target with sibling:** WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR also plans a docs/dev/ test-suite-layout update — coordinate the **Test gates** section (AC6) so the two land without conflicting edits (same file `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` is the likely target).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & decisions

- D1 (decision, from producer record, not a live question): *Should the herdr suite join the canonical full gate?* — **Answer (producer, via WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 closure):** No — "the herdr tests will not be run as part of the canonical full suite — the producer does not want to run the herdr tests." This brief implements the gap the closure left open (sanctioned opt-in type/group + documentation). Research: closure comment on WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 (2026-10-20); suite runtime + flakiness evidence recorded in its intake comment and in WL-0MVFE1IRB0004X1U.
- D2 (assumption, overridable): the named `groups.herdr` (changed-scope auto-selection) is in scope alongside the `types.herdr` map, per the seed intent "Add a herdr test type/group". If the producer prefers type-only, AC2 is dropped and implement.py changed-scope selection is left as-is.

## Related work (find-related automated report)

Automated scan (`find_related.py`, WL-0MVGJ4WSS005BMSI) cross-references:

- **WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR** (open, intake_complete) — *Canonical test suite excludes 76 root-level `tests/*.test.ts` files*: sibling item in the same gap family (different excluded set: root `tests/*` files). Complementary; also references a shared future **Test gates** doc section.
- **WL-0MQDR51JO0037ISJ** (completed) — *Eliminate unsafe as-casts in shortcut dispatch*: tangential, no overlap — excluded-set unrelated; noted for traceability only.
- **WL-0MQOIBGIR006CWLR** (completed) — *Add Background Task Runtime for Non-Blocking Operations*: tangential, no overlap — noted for traceability only.

Repository matches: `packages/herdr/README.md` (already a Key File), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (dispatcher docs, not a gate doc — no change needed), `CLI.md` (CLI docs, no change needed).

## Decompose the `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` god module

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (2,798 lines, 37 exported symbols)

## Problem statement

`packages/herdr/src/index.ts` is the Herdr plugin entry point and has grown to
2,798 lines. It currently carries command routing, argument builders, background
dispatch, pane-ID capture, claim/priority resolution, interactive window and tab
placement, pane cleanup, dozens of production dependency resolvers, the
downtime-worker dependency factory, settings bootstrap and the full TUI
`main()` loop in one module. Navigating, reviewing and safely changing any one
concern requires holding the whole file in view, so every dispatch or TUI change
carries avoidable regression risk.

The 1,000-line maintainability ceiling was adopted for the parent refactor
series WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7. This item is the `index.ts` member of that sweep and
was created specifically to bring this file under the ceiling.

## Users

- **Herdr plugin maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one concern
  (e.g. background dispatch, interactive placement, the TUI loop) without
  reasoning about 2,800 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need a focused diff whose blast radius is legible from
  the touched module.
- **Future agents implementing plugin work items** need small, named modules
  they can locate with a file search instead of reading a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent implementing a background-dispatch change, I want that path in a
  dedicated module so I can modify it without re-reading the TUI loop.
- As a reviewer, I want a split diff attributable to a single concern so I can
  verify it against its own tests.
- As a maintainer, I want each module under 1,000 lines so a file is readable in
  a single pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000
   for `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (now a thin barrel/entry module) and for
   every module created by the split.
2. **Public surface preserved — used symbols only.** Every symbol currently
   imported from `./index.js` by another module remains exported from that exact
   path with identical types and values, so `index.test.ts`, `claim.test.ts`,
   `fetchAuditItemById.test.ts` and `start.ts` compile with no import-path edits.
   The barrel re-exports **only symbols that are actually used** by consumers;
   unused exports stay internal to the extracted modules (inherited producer
   decision Q2 on the parent item, WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7).
3. **Entry-point behaviour preserved.** `start.ts` dynamically imports
   `./index.js` and calls `main()`; `index.ts` keeps exporting `main` and keeps
   the `isEntryPoint` guard so importing the module in a vitest worker still does
   not launch the TUI or call `process.exit`. The entry guard stays in the entry
   module (not in an extracted helper) so `process.argv[1]` identity checks keep
   their current meaning.
4. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change;
   no test file is modified (not its import paths, fixtures or assertions), and
   all `packages/herdr` test suites pass unchanged.
5. **Module-level singletons stay singular.** The `const settings =
   loadSettings()` side effect (currently line 2246) is evaluated **exactly once**
   at module load and shared by `createDowntimeDeps` and `main()`. It must not be
   duplicated into two modules, or the plugin would load settings twice with
   potentially different results. The same rule applies to the resolved script
   paths (`SEND_TO_PI_SCRIPT`, `RUN_IN_PANE_SCRIPT`) which depend on
   `import.meta.url` staying in `packages/herdr/src/`.
6. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `index.js` barrel; the barrel imports downward
   only. The dependency check reports no new cycles (including the existing
   `stalled-work ↔ downtime-worker` type-only cycle, which must not be widened).
7. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, and `npm run build`
   (tsc) must succeed — a module move that breaks the build is not a valid
   intermediate state.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and update imports; do not refactor logic, rename
  public symbols, or change behaviour.
- **Barrel compatibility.** 3 test files and `start.ts` import from
  `./index.js`; the barrel preserves that contract (AC2/AC3).
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf modules first and work inwards,
  so each merged step leaves the build and the full suite green.
- **No new runtime dependencies**, no test-file rewrites, no changes to the wl
  CLI contract or to plugin behaviour.
- **Scope boundary.** This item targets `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` only. Test
  file size (`index.test.ts` is 3,977 lines), sibling production files and a
  repo-wide lint rule are out of scope (see Risks — scope creep).

## Existing state

`index.ts` is 2,798 lines. Its cohesive sections (line ranges from the current
`dev` checkout) are:

| # | Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---------|-------|------|
| 1 | Header, imports and resolved script paths | 1–174 | 174 |
| 2 | Command routing + arg builders (`routeCommand`, `stripCommandPrefix`, `buildSendToPiArgs`, `buildRunInPaneArgs`, `parsePaneIdFile`) | 176–376 | 201 |
| 3 | Background (no-pane) dispatch (`BACKGROUND_LOG_DIR`, log helpers, `spawnBackgroundShell`, `spawnBackgroundPi`) | 377–579 | 203 |
| 4 | Pane-ID capture + work-item extraction (`CAPTURE_*`, `capturePaneIdFromFile`, `extractWorkItemId`) | 580–675 | 96 |
| 5 | Claim + interactive priority (`claimItemForAgentCommand`, `resolveInteractiveDispatchPriority`, priority lookup, critical blockers) | 676–794 | 119 |
| 6 | Default anchor resolvers (dispatcher/project/tab/item, internal) | 795–895 | 101 |
| 7 | Interactive placement + root-pane cleanup (`resolveInteractiveWorkspaceId`, `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor`, `closeInteractiveTabRootPane`, `defaultInteractiveLiveTrackedPanesResolver`, `defaultInteractiveClosePane`) | 896–1111 | 216 |
| 8 | Downtime/stalled resolvers (`defaultRunningDowntimePanesResolver`, `defaultStalledResume*`, `defaultStalledPanesLister`, `worklogRootFromPiSessionPath`, `defaultStalledPaneRootResolver`, `readClosedPaneIds`) | 1112–1319 | 208 |
| 9 | `createDowntimeDeps` dependency factory | 1323–2244 | 922 |
| 10 | Settings bootstrap (`const settings = loadSettings()`) | 2246 | 1 |
| 11 | Worklog target configuration (`configureWorklogTarget`, `uninitializedReport`) | 2261–2283 | 23 |
| 12 | TUI `main()` loop | 2284–2783 | 500 |
| 13 | Entry-point guard (`isEntryPoint` + `main().catch`) | 2785–2798 | 14 |

Relevant structural facts discovered during intake:

- **Used public surface (26 symbols):** static imports from `./index.js` are
  `stripCommandPrefix`, `routeCommand`, `stripAgentPromptPrefix`,
  `buildSendToPiArgs`, `buildRunInPaneArgs`, `createDowntimeDeps`,
  `capturePaneIdFromFile`, `parsePaneIdFile`, `buildBackgroundLogPath`,
  `spawnBackgroundShell`, `spawnBackgroundPi`, `formatBackgroundFailure`,
  `CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `extractWorkItemId`, `defaultStalledPaneRootResolver`,
  `defaultStalledPanesLister`, `worklogRootFromPiSessionPath`,
  `resolveInteractiveDispatchPriority`, `claimItemForAgentCommand`; dynamic
  `import('./index.js')` in `index.test.ts` additionally uses
  `configureWorklogTarget`, `uninitializedReport`,
  `defaultInteractiveLiveTrackedPanesResolver`, `resolveInteractiveWorkspaceId`,
  `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor`, `closeInteractiveTabRootPane`; `start.ts`
  dynamically uses `main`.
- **Unused exported symbols (safe to keep internal):** `CommandRoute`,
  `BACKGROUND_LOG_DIR`, `BackgroundSpawnDeps`, `CAPTURE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`,
  `PaneIdFileDeps`, `InteractiveLiveTrackedPanesResult`,
  `InteractiveRootPaneCleanupDeps`, `defaultInteractiveClosePane`,
  `defaultRunningDowntimePanesResolver`, `defaultStalledResumePromptAgent`,
  `defaultStalledResumeStartAgent`.
- **Single module-level side effect:** `const settings = loadSettings()` at line
  2246, read by `createDowntimeDeps` (line 2144) and `main()`. No other top-level
  statements exist beyond the entry guard.
- **Entry point chain:** `herdr-plugin.toml` launches
  `npx tsx src/start.ts`; `start.ts` dynamically imports `./index.js` and calls
  `main()`. The `isEntryPoint` guard in both modules prevents test-time launch.
- **Test gate:** `index.test.ts` (3,977 lines), `claim.test.ts` (407), and
  `fetchAuditItemById.test.ts` (281) import the module and must stay unmodified.
- **Precedent:** WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO decomposed the 2,584-line
  `src/database.ts` god class under ACs requiring an unchanged public API,
  tests passing without modification, and per-module line ceilings.
- **Parent decisions inherited:** scope limited to this file with follow-up items
  for the rest (Q1 → A); keep a public barrel re-exporting used symbols only
  (Q2 → A refined); delivery as an epic decomposed into sequenced child items,
  leaf-first (Q3 → A). See WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 Appendix.

## Desired change

Reduce `index.ts` to a thin re-export barrel plus the entry-point guard and
shared bootstrap side effect, and move its contents into cohesive sibling
modules. A starting decomposition (boundaries are an implementation decision,
subject to the constraints above):

| New module | Responsibility | Approx. size |
|---|---|---|
| `index.commands.ts` | `routeCommand`, `stripCommandPrefix`, `buildSendToPiArgs`, `buildRunInPaneArgs`, `parsePaneIdFile` and command-prefix helpers | ~210 |
| `index.background.ts` | Background (no-pane) dispatch: log paths, failure formatting, `spawnBackgroundShell`, `spawnBackgroundPi` | ~205 |
| `index.pane-capture.ts` | `capturePaneIdFromFile`, capture constants, `extractWorkItemId` | ~100 |
| `index.claim.ts` | `claimItemForAgentCommand`, interactive dispatch priority and critical-blocker lookup | ~120 |
| `index.interactive.ts` | Interactive workspace/item anchor resolution, tab root-pane cleanup and live-tracked-pane resolvers | ~220 |
| `index.resolvers.ts` | Production default resolvers for dispatcher/project/item anchors, running downtime panes, stalled panes and worklog root | ~310 |
| `index.downtime-deps.ts` | `createDowntimeDeps` and its internal helpers (includes the `fetchAuditItemById` closure) | ~925 |
| `index.settings.ts` | Single `settings = loadSettings()` instance and `configureWorklogTarget`/`uninitializedReport` bootstrap helpers | ~30 |
| `index.main.ts` | The TUI `main()` loop | ~505 |
| `index.ts` | Thin barrel re-exporting used symbols + entry-point guard | ~120–200 |

If any candidate module still exceeds the ceiling, it is split further along the
section boundary rather than left oversized. `createDowntimeDeps` is the largest
single unit (922 lines) and may need its `fetchAuditItemById` closure extracted to
stay clearly under the limit.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — reduce to a thin barrel + entry-point guard; preserve every used export.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.commands.ts` — new; command routing and argument builders.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.background.ts` — new; background dispatch and log handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.pane-capture.ts` — new; pane-ID capture and work-item extraction.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.claim.ts` — new; claim and interactive priority.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.interactive.ts` — new; interactive placement and pane cleanup.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.resolvers.ts` — new; default dependency resolvers.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.downtime-deps.ts` — new; `createDowntimeDeps` factory.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.settings.ts` — new; single settings instance and bootstrap helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.main.ts` — new; TUI `main()` loop.
- `packages/herdr/src/start.ts`, `index.test.ts`, `claim.test.ts`, `fetchAuditItemById.test.ts` — must remain unmodified; they are the behaviour-preservation gate.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — module-layout note pointing at the new files.
- `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md` — update the `index.ts` production-wiring reference if paths move.
- `docs/dev/rca-downtime-3-consecutive-wl-cli-errors.md` — update the `createDowntimeDeps` file reference if it moves.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7** — *downtime-worker.ts is a god class* (parent refactor series; discovered-from). Source of the 1,000-line sweep and the producer's Q1–Q3 decisions.
- **WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO** — *Decompose WorklogDatabase god class (src/database.ts, 2,584 lines)* (completed). Direct precedent: same refactor shape, same AC pattern.
- **WL-0MQRVM54T006WQ20** — *Fix piman.ts extension path after index.ts removal* (completed). Prior change to this entry point's path resolution.
- **WL-0MQRU076X0050VNB** — *Fix duplicate extension load caused by re-export shim* (completed). Relevant caution: a re-export shim previously caused a duplicate extension load.
- **WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B** — *Refactor: decompose packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts god class* (in progress). Sibling refactor item.
- **WL-0MT2GITCX009WUEW** — *Remove packages/herdr/src/icons.ts and rewire herdr consumers* (completed). Related herdr consumer-rewiring precedent.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — herdr package overview; documents the entry point.
- `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md` — describes the production wiring in `index.ts`.
- `docs/dev/rca-downtime-3-consecutive-wl-cli-errors.md` — references `createDowntimeDeps` in `index.ts`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MT2GITCX009WUEW** – Remove packages/herdr/src/icons.ts and rewire herdr consumers (completed)
- **WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4** – herdr plugin crashes at startup: Cannot find package 'marked' (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND) (completed)
- **WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ** – Refactor: decompose src/sync.ts god class (goal: no file > 1000 lines) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
- `CLI.md`

## Risks and assumptions

- **Barrel-induced runtime cycle (medium).** A module that imports from
  `index.js` would create a cycle through the barrel. *Mitigation:* extracted
  modules import only concrete siblings; the barrel imports downward only
  (AC6).
- **Duplicate settings load (medium).** `const settings = loadSettings()` must
  live in exactly one module. *Mitigation:* AC5; keep it in a leaf
  `index.settings.ts` consumed by both `createDowntimeDeps` and `main()`.
- **Broken entry point (high).** `start.ts` imports `main()` and the
  `isEntryPoint` guard depends on `process.argv[1]`. *Mitigation:* AC3 keeps
  `main` and the guard in `index.ts`; the plugin-startup tests and
  `vitest run` on `index.test.ts` are the gate.
- **Lost provenance / accidental logic drift (medium).** A large move invites
  silent edits. *Mitigation:* move-only rule, unchanged test suite (AC4), and a
  review pass that diffs moved blocks against the original.
- **Test-file temptation (low).** Updating `index.test.ts` import paths is the
  easy path but erases the behaviour-preservation signal. *Mitigation:* AC2/AC4
  make unchanged tests a hard gate.
- **`index.test.ts` is also over 1,000 lines (1,977 lines over).** It is
  explicitly out of scope here (test files were evaluated in lockstep with their
  module, not filed as standalone items). Recorded as a known follow-up
  opportunity, not absorbed into this item. *Mitigation:* note it in the plan
  and, if the producer wants it, file a separate test-decomposition item.
- **Scope-creep risk (explicit).** Splitting sibling files, adding a lint rule
  for file length, or refactoring behaviour are out of scope; each is recorded
  as a linked follow-up rather than absorbed here.

## Assumptions

- Each sequenced child lands tree-green: `npm run build` succeeds and the full
  suite passes before the next child starts.
- The decomposition will be delivered as an epic with sequenced child items (one
  per extracted module), landed leaf-first and independently green (parent Q3).
- The barrel re-exports only the symbols consumers use; unused exports become
  internal (parent Q2).
- `index.test.ts`, `claim.test.ts`, `fetchAuditItemById.test.ts` and `start.ts`
  remain unmodified.
- The `createDowntimeDeps` closure `fetchAuditItemById` may need extraction to
  keep its module under the ceiling; that is an implementation decision, not a
  behaviour change.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Inherited from the parent item (WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7) — no new questions
blocking:**

- Q (scope): Is the "no file > 1,000 lines" goal limited to this file, or should
  other `packages/herdr` files be split too? — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-20):
  A** — limit to this file; follow-up items for the rest; add the >1,000-line
  check to the refactor skill. Source: parent Appendix Q1.
- Q (compatibility): Keep a public barrel re-exporting the current surface, or
  update importers? — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-20): A, refined** — keep the
  barrel, but re-export only symbols actually used. Source: parent Appendix Q2.
- Q (delivery shape): One big-bang change or an epic with sequenced children? —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-10-20): A** — epic with sequenced children, leaf
  modules first, blocking order. Source: parent Appendix Q3.

**Resolved by repository inspection (no producer answer required):**

- Q: How large is the file and what are its cohesive sections? — Answer: 2,798
  lines across 13 logical sections (inventory above). Source: `wc -l` and export
  scan of `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`.
- Q: How many consumers depend on its public surface? — Answer: 3 test files
  (`index.test.ts`, `claim.test.ts`, `fetchAuditItemById.test.ts`) and
  `start.ts`; 26 symbols are actually used. Source: import scan of
  `packages/herdr/src/*.ts`.
- Q: Is there module-level mutable state that a split could duplicate? — Answer:
  yes, `const settings = loadSettings()` (line 2246), read by
  `createDowntimeDeps` and `main()`. Source: line scan of the file.
- Q: What is the entry-point contract? — Answer: `herdr-plugin.toml` launches
  `src/start.ts`, which dynamically imports `./index.js` and calls `main()`; an
  `isEntryPoint` guard prevents test-time launch. Source:
  `packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml`, `packages/herdr/src/start.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (line 2785).
- Q: Is there an existing import cycle to preserve carefully? — Answer: a
  type-only `stalled-work ↔ downtime-worker` cycle exists at the package level;
  this split must not widen it. Source: imports in both files (inherited
  parent finding).
- Q: Is `index.test.ts` in scope? — Answer: no; test files are evaluated in
  lockstep with their module and are not standalone refactor items (parent
  note). It stays unmodified as the behaviour-preservation gate. Source: parent
  description, `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` size.

# Herdr: coalesce the per-refresh `wl` spawns into one consolidated read

## Problem statement

A Herdr default-view refresh runs **five separate `wl` subprocesses per pane per tick**: the four mandatory `wl list` subsets plus the `wl next` browse feed (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`). Per-spawn Node bootstrap now dominates the cost (~66 % of the remaining 0.70 CPU-s/spawn is the bare-node floor), so F10 capped the achievable reduction at ~65 % with five spawns and missed the 60 % target (47.6 % achieved). The remaining lever is **fewer spawns**: one consolidated read per refresh tick.

## Users

- **Herdr pane operator** (producer/agent running several Herdr panes on one worklog): wants a responsive worklist without each pane burning CPU on five `wl` boots per tick.
- **Herdr plugin maintainer**: wants one simple, cacheable read seam instead of five coordinated queries with an in-flight memo.
- **wl CLI maintainer**: wants the consolidated command to reuse the existing DB-query and read-cache machinery, not fork it.

### Example user stories

- As a Herdr pane operator, when 4–5 panes refresh every 30 s against one shared worklog, total CPU consumption should drop to **≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline** so the host stays responsive.
- As a Herdr plugin maintainer, I want `fetcher.ts` to issue **one `wl` read per refresh tick** (one DB open, one cache entry), with the displayed items unchanged.
- As an agent relying on the worklist, I want the **mandatory guarantees** (critical items, blocked items and the review queue always shown) preserved by tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A single `wl` invocation returns every subset the worklist needs — critical, in_review review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots and the browse feed — as a **dedicated `wl worklist --json` command** (preferred) or an equivalent `--worklist-bundle` mode, sharing **one DB open and one read-cache entry**.
2. `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` issues that single read per default-view refresh tick; the mandatory-subset guarantees (critical always shown, blocked always shown, review queue always shown) are preserved by tests.
3. Measured with `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10): total CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle with 4 panes drops to **≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline (≤ 63.8 CPU-s)**, ideally ~5× fewer spawns.
4. Cache correctness unchanged: identical JSON for identical DB state, write invalidation still bumps the state counter, and worktree / `--worklog-dir` behaviour is unchanged.
5. Herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state (existing fetcher tests + the spawn-reduction simulation pass).
6. **Testing/validation:** new tests cover the consolidated command's response shape, read-cache hit and write-invalidation, the fetcher's single-spawn path, mandatory-subset guarantees and output parity with the per-subset path.
7. **Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (notably `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`).
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Pure read:** the bundle must not write. `wl next`'s auto re-sort is a write byproduct; the bundle must use `--no-re-sort`-style selection (or reuse the selection logic without the write) so the result is deterministically cacheable.
- **Cache reuse:** register the new invocation with the existing read-cache (`src/read-cache-cli.ts`), keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)` and fingerprinted by the monotonic state counter; a mid-action write must not cache an unrepresentative payload.
- **Fail-open fallback:** if the consolidated read is unavailable or fails (older `wl`, malformed payload), the fetcher falls back to today's per-subset spawn path with unchanged behaviour.
- **No output change:** the consolidated response must feed the same `extractItems` → `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems` pipeline so ordering, grouping and audit enrichment are identical.
- **Bounded payload:** the browse feed stays limited by the caller's count; subsets are returned with the same filters (`--root-only` where applicable) so payload growth is bounded and no item duplication is unbounded.
- `--worklog-dir` (module override and per-call) and managed-worktree resolution semantics are unchanged.
- TypeScript/Node stack; match existing style; no new runtime dependency unless unavoidable.

## Existing state

- **fetcher.ts** — `fetchMandatorySubsets()` spawns four `wl list` queries in parallel (critical, review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots); `fetchNextItems()` spawns `wl next` and calls `fetchMandatorySubsets()`, giving five spawns per default-view refresh. An in-flight fetch memo deduplicates *identical* concurrent reads (which collapses the review-queue state query into the review subset), and `fetchChildrenForItems` / `fetchActionableCount` already read in-process from SQLite via one refresh-scoped connection.
- **Read cache** — `src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts` serve `list`, `next`, `show`, `search` and `status` JSON from a shared on-disk cache keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)`, fingerprinted by a monotonic per-worklog-dir write counter; writes bump the counter and drop entries. `src/cli.ts` performs the lookup before loading the heavy command graph.
- **CLI commands** — `src/commands/*.ts` register subcommands through `src/plugin-types.ts` / `src/command-registry.ts`; `next.ts` owns the auto re-sort and the selection semantics; `list.ts` owns the filtered list queries.
- **Measurement** — `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10, 4 panes × 30 s × 5 s tick, sums per-process CPU from spawn records) and `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` (spawn-count/latency per refresh).
- **F10 numbers** — pre-F4 baseline 159.44 CPU-s/cycle, after F4–F7 83.58 CPU-s/cycle (47.6 % reduction), target 63.78; per-spawn 1.329 → 0.697 CPU-s against a ~0.46 CPU-s bare-node floor.

## Desired change

1. Add a consolidated worklist read to the `wl` CLI — preferably a new `wl worklist --json` command — that opens the database **once** and returns the critical, review-queue, in-progress-root, blocked-root and browse-feed subsets in one payload, built from the same query/selection code the individual commands use.
2. Make it a cacheable read invocation (one cache entry, same state-counter fingerprint and write invalidation), so repeat refreshes across panes hit the cache as a single entry.
3. Change `fetcher.ts` so the default-view refresh drives that one read (with the review-queue state and browse feed derived from it) and retains the existing per-subset path as a fail-open fallback.
4. Add coverage: command unit/integration tests, cache hit/invalidation tests, fetcher single-spawn and mandatory-guarantee tests, and an output-parity test against the per-subset path; update the spawn-reduction simulation and the benchmark expectations.
5. Update `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` and any CLI reference docs/comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — **new** consolidated read command (or a `--worklist-bundle` mode added to `src/commands/list.ts`)
- `src/command-registry.ts` — register the new command
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — add the invocation to `READ_CACHE_COMMANDS` / cacheability checks
- `src/cli.ts` — cache lookup path (expected unchanged; verify the new command is served before the heavy graph)
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — single consolidated read, review-state/browse derivation, fail-open fallback
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `doRefresh` wiring so the bundle replaces the per-subset fan-out
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` — spawn-reduction simulation uses the consolidated invocation
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-*.test.ts` — mandatory-subset, review-queue and output-parity coverage
- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` — measurement harness (expects the consolidated query)
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — cold-refresh cost section updated

## Related work

- **F10 — WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J** (completed): measured the <= 60 % shortfall and filed this item with the spawn-count lever. This item is the follow-up implementation of that lever.
- **WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B** (completed, outbound dependency): spawn-load epic — transient `wl` process CPU usage.
- **WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG** (completed): cut cold refresh cost — in-process SQLite reads, in-flight fetch memo, batched expanded children. The consolidated read builds on this.
- **WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B** (completed): one shared in-process connection per refresh — related "one open per refresh" precedent.
- **WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN** (completed): make Herdr refresh snappy after agent updates — parent of the earlier performance work.
- **Docs:** `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`, `docs/dev/wl-spawn-baseline-2026-10-19.md`, `docs/benchmarks/wal-read-latency-benchmark.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Cache staleness (risk, high):** a single cache entry must never serve stale data across a write. Mitigation: reuse the counter fingerprint, cache only when the counter is unchanged since lookup, and add an explicit write-invalidation test.
- **Re-sort write byproduct (risk, medium):** today's `wl next` runs an auto re-sort (a DB write) on some invocations. The bundle must be a pure read; assumption: `--no-re-sort` selection produces the same displayed order for a stable DB. Verify with an output-parity test; if ordering genuinely differs, resolve the re-sort as a separate, explicitly-documented concern rather than making the bundle a write.
- **Mandatory-subset regression (risk, high):** a bundle that silently drops a subset breaks the always-shown guarantees. Mitigation: tests assert each mandatory subset is present regardless of the browse window.
- **Backwards compatibility (risk, low):** an older `wl` without the new command. Mitigation: fall back to the per-subset spawn path (fail-open).
- **Cross-subset consistency (risk, medium):** the five subsets are read in one process but through separate queries; a write landing mid-bundle could make the subsets disagree. Mitigation: serve all subsets from one DB connection inside a read transaction (or the same store snapshot) so the payload reflects one stable state; at minimum, match today's eventual-consistency behaviour and document it.
- **Payload size (risk, low):** five subsets in one payload. Mitigation: keep the browse feed count-bounded and reuse the existing dedupe/merge pipeline.
- **Scope creep (risk, medium):** further per-spawn startup optimisation (F4–F7) is out of scope. Record additional opportunities as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption:** `wl` and the Herdr plugin ship together from this repository, so the fetcher may rely on the new command in the same release; the fallback remains for robustness.

## Verification plan

```sh
# CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle, 4 panes (F10 harness)
npm run benchmark:herdr-refresh -- --json --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5

# Spawn count and latency for a single default-view refresh
npx tsx bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts --json
```

- Compare the measured CPU-seconds against the ≤ 63.8 CPU-s target and the pre-F4 baseline quoted above.
- Run the changed-scope and full test suites via `/skill:test`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Was an interview needed for this intake?
  **A (agent, based on repo evidence):** No. The seed context already contains a measured problem, a quantified target, explicit acceptance criteria and a named lever, so the brief was drafted directly from that plus a repo inspection. Source: work item description and F10 comment.
- **Q:** Which command shape should the consolidated read take?
  **A (agent, derived from work item AC):** The AC permits either a `--worklist-bundle` mode or a dedicated command; this brief records a dedicated `wl worklist --json` command as the preferred option (cleaner cache key, no change to `list`/`next` semantics). Source: work item AC 1.
- **Q:** Does the browse feed's auto re-sort write belong in the bundle?
  **A (agent, derived from `src/commands/next.ts`):** The bundle must be a pure read to be deterministically cacheable, so it uses `--no-re-sort`-style selection and the re-sort is treated as a separate concern; output parity is guarded by a test. Recorded as a risk above. Source: `src/commands/next.ts` auto re-sort logic.
- **Q:** Is a fail-open fallback required?
  **A (agent, derived from existing fetcher design):** Yes — the fetcher's existing in-process fast paths all fail open to `wl` spawns; the consolidated read follows the same convention. Source: `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J** – Verify >=60% CPU-second reduction per refresh cycle (completed)
- **WL-0MSHJ2NWZ000P3X9** – [test-failure] read-cache spawn reduction (6-pane simulation) cuts work spawns by ≥60% across a simulated 6-pane refresh — failing test (completed)
- **WL-0MVFRR98A008MM19** – Spawn instrumentation: per-process CPU and RSS (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, always, bare, baseline, behaviour (+101 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: always, bare, baseline, behaviour, bench (+92 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: achieved, always, bare, behaviour, blocked (+86 more)

## Failure Signature

- Test file: `tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts`
- Test case: `entry-point split — fast path > records --version as a version spawn and prints the package version`
- Failure: `AssertionError: --version must record exactly one version spawn record: expected +0 to be 1`

## Root Cause (investigated by plan)

`tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts` selects its CLI under test with
`resolveStartupTarget('auto', repoRoot)` (see `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts`).
`auto` **prefers `dist/cli.js` when that built file exists**, falling back to
`src/cli.ts` only on an unbuilt checkout.

The checked-out `dist/cli.js` was built at **2026-10-19 21:21**, before
commit `896d8ad2` (WL-0MVFRRGGC001IQK1, 2026-10-20 04:59) added the
`--version` spawn instrumentation to `src/cli.ts`:

```ts
// src/cli.ts:568-570
if (!cacheServed && (cacheArgv.includes('--version') || cacheArgv.includes('-V'))) {
  recordSpawn('version');
}
```

The stale `dist/cli.js` has `recordSpawn('read-work')` but **no
`recordSpawn('version')`** call, so the spawned CLI records no `version`
spawn record and the assertion `expected +0 to be 1` fires.

`dist/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:86`) and `npm test` does not rebuild it,
so any checkout whose `dist/` predates the `src/` change exhibits this
failure even though the source is correct.

**Conclusion:** the source is correct; the observed failure is a stale-build
artefact of the `auto` target selection, not a source defect.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. From a checkout where `dist/cli.js` predates the `src/cli.ts` version
   instrumentation (`git log --oneline -1 -- src/cli.ts` newer than the
   mtime of `dist/cli.js`):
   - `npx vitest run tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts -t 'records --version as a version spawn'`
2. Observe: `expected +0 to be 1`.
3. Rebuild the CLI (`npm run build`) and re-run the same test — it passes.

## Candidate Remediations (for implementation)

- **A — Rebuild before testing (primary):** ensure `dist/cli.js` is rebuilt
  from HEAD before the suite runs, so `auto` never selects a stale build.
  Preferred fix is that the test/CI path rebuilds (or the test verifies build
  freshness) rather than relying on a manually-built `dist`.
- **B — Fail loudly on stale dist:** make `resolveStartupTarget('auto', …)`
  (or the test setup) detect a `dist/cli.js` older than the newest `src/**`
  file and either rebuild or fall back to `src`, so a stale build cannot
  silently produce a false test failure.
- **C — Test-only hardening:** assert build freshness in
  `entry-point-split.test.ts` so the failure message names the stale build
  instead of the downstream spawn-count assertion.

Remediation A is the minimum end-to-end slice; B prevents recurrence for all
tests that use `auto`.

## Impact

Failing test detected during an automated run. Blocks a green suite for the
agent's current work item and can block PR creation. Not a product defect
once `dist/cli.js` is current.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npx vitest run tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts` passes against the
   latest `dev` with `dist/cli.js` rebuilt from HEAD (`auto` target).
2. The chosen remediation prevents recurrence: a stale `dist/cli.js` either
   cannot be selected by the `auto` target or produces an explicit
   stale-build failure rather than a misleading spawn-count assertion.
3. Any documentation describing the test/benchmark `auto`/`dist`/`src`
   target selection is updated to note the build-freshness requirement.
4. Full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Links

- Test: `tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts`
- Target selection: `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` (`resolveStartupTarget`)
- Version instrumentation: `src/cli.ts:568-570`, `src/spawn-counter.ts`
- Predecessor commit introducing the instrumentation: `896d8ad2`
- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md

## Key Files

- `tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts`
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` (`resolveStartupTarget`)
- `docs/dev/wl-startup-import-budget.md` (AC3 docs update)
- `src/cli.ts` (reference only — no change expected; source already correct)

Approach: the suite-speed epic (WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8, commit 1648fa1b) had already converted this test to the pre-compiled CLI bundle (tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts → runCliProcess): same src/cli.ts command graph including the read-cache fast path, ~1.3 s per spawn vs tsx's 2.5–8 s.
